questions.explanation:
Why This Is Asked

Tests practical, auditable governance for multi-team clusters beyond image/security gates.

Key Concepts

- Namespace governance with ResourceQuota and LimitRange
- Namespace-scoped RBAC and ServiceAccounts
- Lightweight CI gates using kubectl/yq
- Local validation vs CI parity

Code Example

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
for ns in $(kubectl get ns -o jsonpath='{.items[*].metadata.name}'); do
  kubectl -n "$ns" get resourcequota >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "Missing ResourceQuota in $ns"; exit 1; }
  kubectl -n "$ns" get limitrange >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "Missing LimitRange in $ns"; exit 1; }
  for dep in $(kubectl -n "$ns" get deploy -o jsonpath='{range .items[*]}{.metadata.name} {/end}'); do
    sa=$(kubectl -n "$ns" get deploy "$dep" -o jsonpath='{.spec.template.spec.serviceAccountName}')
    if [ -z "$sa" ]; then echo "Deployment $dep in $ns uses default SA"; exit 1; fi
    kubectl -n "$ns" get rolebinding | grep -q "$sa" || { echo "Missing RBAC for $sa in $ns"; exit 1; }
  done
done
```

Failing manifest

```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Namespace
metadata:
  name: team-a
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: app
  namespace: team-a
spec:
  replicas: 1
  template:
    metadata:
      name: app
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: app
        image: nginx:latest
```

Passing manifest

```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Namespace
metadata:
  name: team-a
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: ResourceQuota
metadata:
  name: rq
  namespace: team-a
spec:
  hard:
    requests.cpu: "4"
    limits.cpu: "8"
    requests.memory: 8Gi
    limits.memory: 16Gi
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: LimitRange
metadata:
  name: lr
  namespace: team-a
spec:
  limits:
  - max:
      cpu: "4"
      memory: 8Gi
    min:
      cpu: 100m
      memory: 128Mi
    default:
      cpu: 500m
      memory: 512Mi
    defaultRequest:
      cpu: 100m
      memory: 128Mi
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: ServiceAccount
metadata:
  name: sa-team-a
  namespace: team-a
---
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: RoleBinding
metadata:
  name: sa-team-a-view
  namespace: team-a
subjects:
- kind: ServiceAccount
  name: sa-team-a
  namespace: team-a
roleRef:
  kind: ClusterRole
  name: view
  apiGroup: rbac.authorization.k8s.io
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: app
  namespace: team-a
spec:
  replicas: 1
  template:
    metadata:
      name: app
    spec:
      serviceAccountName: sa-team-a
      containers:
      - name: app
        image: nginx:1.21
```

Verification

- Locally: run the gate script against your cluster context and verify it fails/passes as expected; inspect output for missing quota/limitrange or RBAC gaps.
- CI: run the same script in a workflow step; ensure failing manifests fail the build and passing manifests pass.

## Why This Is Asked

Tests basic security gating in a beginner-friendly way that ties manifest hardening to CI.

- Kubernetes securityContext fields
- kube-score risk levels (low/medium/high/critical)
- CI gate integration and failure semantics

## Code Example

```yaml

kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: insecure-pod
spec:
  containers:
  - name: app
    image: alpine:3.18
    securityContext:
      runAsNonRoot: false
      privileged: true
      readOnlyRootFilesystem: false
```

```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: secure-pod
spec:
  containers:
  - name: app
    image: alpine:3.18
    securityContext:
      runAsNonRoot: true
      runAsUser: 1000
      privileged: false
      readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
      allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
```

```yaml
name: kube-score gate
on:
  push:
  pull_request:

jobs:
  kube-score:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Install kube-score
        run: |
          curl -L -o kube-score https://github.com/zegl/kube-score/releases/download/v1.9.0/kube-score-1.9.0-linux-amd64
          chmod +x kube-score
          sudo mv kube-score /usr/local/bin/kube-score
      - name: Run kube-score
        run: kube-score score manifests/ --output json > kube-score.json
      - name: Fail on high risk
        run: |
          if grep -q high kube-score.json || grep -q critical kube-score.json; then
            echo High-risk issues found
            exit 1
          fi
```

- How would you scale this to multiple repos?
- How would you handle false positives?

## Why This Is Asked

Tests ability to design runtime security controls that span CI, policy engines, and multi cloud networking, ensuring outbound traffic is strictly controlled and auditable.

## Key Concepts

- Policy-as-code (Gatekeeper/OPA)
- Egress gateway design and TLS origination
- Outbound allowlist management
- CI validation for policy enforcement
- Cross-cloud consistency and testing

## Code Example

```yaml
# ConstraintTemplate for Gatekeeper enforcing egress gateway annotation
apiVersion: templates.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: ConstraintTemplate
metadata:
  name: k8segressgateway
spec:
  crd:
    spec:
      names:
        kind: K8sEgressPolicy
  targets:
  - target: obj  # pseudo example for clarity
    rego: |
      package k8segress
      default deny = true
      deny[msg] = msg {
        input.review.kind.kind == "Pod"
        not input.review.object.metadata.annotations["egress.gateway/enforced"] == "true"
        msg := "Pod must set egress.gateway/enforced=true to route via central gateway"
      }
```

```yaml
# Constraint demonstrating allowlist usage (illustrative)
apiVersion: constraints.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: K8sEgressPolicy
metadata:
  name: require-egress-gateway
spec:
  match:
    kinds:
      - apiGroups: [""]
        kinds: ["Pod"]
  parameters:
    allowlist: ["app.allowed.example.com"]
```

```yaml
# Failing manifest (no egress annotation or disallowed destination)
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: bad-egress-pod
  annotations:
    # missing or false
    egress.gateway/enforced: "false"
spec:
  containers:
  - name: app
    image: nginx:latest
```

```yaml
# Passing manifest (annotation set and allowlisted destination)
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: good-egress-pod
  annotations:
    egress.gateway/enforced: "true"
spec:
  containers:
  - name: app
    image: nginx:1.23.4
```

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Real-world security requires automated SBOMs and multi-tool vulnerability checks to prevent risky images from entering registries.

## Key Concepts
- SBOM generation with Syft
- Parallel scans with Trivy and Grype
- PR gating and artifact attachment
- Validation in CI and via PR comments

## Code Example
```yaml
# minimal GitHub Actions workflow (yaml)
name: SBOM and vulnerability gate
on:
  pull_request:
    types: [opened, synchronize]
jobs:
  gate:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Build image
        run: |
          docker build -t myimage:${{ github.sha }} .
      - name: Generate SBOM
        run: |
          docker run --rm -v /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock anchore/syft:latest DockerImage:${{ github.sha }} -o json > sbom.json
      - name: Scan with Trivy
        run: |
          docker run --rm -v /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock aquasecurity/trivy:latest image --exit-code 1 --no-progress myimage:${{ github.sha }} || true
      - name: Scan with Grype
        run: |
          grype myimage:${{ github.sha }} -o json > grype.json || true
      - name: Upload SBOMs
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v3
        with:
          name: sboms
          path: sbom.json, grype.json
      - name: Fail if CVEs found
        run: |
          if [ -s grype.json ] && grep -q '"score": 7' grype.json; then exit 1; fi
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you adapt this gate for a multi-arch build?
- How would you integrate SBOM attestation into your registry metadata?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked

Real-world cross-cloud serverless platforms demand automated image signing and artifact attestations. This question tests end-to-end workflow design, policy enforcement decisions, and practical CI/CD integration skills.

## Key Concepts

- Cosign signing and verification
- Rekor attestations for transparency and auditability
- SBOM generation (using tools like Syft)
- Multi-cloud serverless deployment patterns
- GitHub Actions workflow integration

## Code Example

```yaml
name: cks-serverless-sign
on:
  pull_request:
    types: [opened, synchronize]

jobs:
  gate:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Install cosign
        uses: sigstore/cosign-installer@v3

      - name: Set up Syft for SBOM
        uses: anchore/syft-action@v1

      - name: Build and push image
        run: |
          docker build -t ${{ vars.REGISTRY }}/serverless-fn:${{ github.sha }} .
          docker push ${{ vars.REGISTRY }}/serverless-fn:${{ github.sha }}

      - name: Generate SBOM
        run: |
          syft ${{ vars.REGISTRY }}/serverless-fn:${{ github.sha }} -o cyclonedx-json > sbom.json

      - name: Sign image with cosign
        run: |
          cosign sign --key cosign.key ${{ vars.REGISTRY }}/serverless-fn:${{ github.sha }}

      - name: Verify signature
        run: |
          cosign verify --key cosign.pub ${{ vars.REGISTRY }}/serverless-fn:${{ github.sha }}

      - name: Upload to Rekor
        run: |
          cosign upload blob -f attestation.json
```

## Failing Manifest (Unsigned Image)

```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: serverless-workload
spec:
  containers:
  - name: function
    image: registry.example.com/serverless-fn:abc123
```

## Passing Manifest (Signed Image)

```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: serverless-workload
spec:
  containers:
  - name: function
    image: registry.example.com/serverless-fn:signed-sha256
    imagePullPolicy: Always
```

## Local Verification

```bash
# Verify image signature
cosign verify --key cosign.pub registry.example.com/serverless-fn:signed-sha256

# Verify attestation
cosign verify-attestation --type cyclonedx --key cosign.pub registry.example.com/serverless-fn:signed-sha256
```

## CI Verification Steps

1. Add Cosign verification step in CI pipeline
2. Block deployment if signature verification fails
3. Verify SBOM matches image contents
4. Check Rekor transparency log for attestation

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests end-to-end security for ML artifacts, combining signing attestations, GitOps, and runtime policy in Kubernetes.

## Key Concepts
- Sigstore Cosign sign-blob attest and verify-blob
- Model provenance and SBOM
- GitOps with Argo CD
- Admission policies: OPA Gatekeeper or Kyverno

## Code Example
```bash
# Sign a model blob and create an attestation
cosign sign-blob -key cosign.key models/model-v1.bin
cosign attest -key cosign.key --predicate predicate.json models/model-v1.bin
cosign verify-blob -key cosign.pub models/model-v1.bin
```

```yaml
# Kyverno policy requiring attestation before deployment
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: require-model-attestation
spec:
  validationFailureAction: enforce
  rules:
  - name: attested-model-artifact
    match:
      resources:
        kinds: [Deployment]
    validate:
      message: Attestation required for model artifact
      pattern:
        metadata.annotations.cosign_attested: "true"
```

```rego
package kubernetes.admission

deny[{"msg": msg}] {
  input.request.kind.kind == "Deployment"
  not input.request.object.metadata.annotations["cosign_attested"] == "true"
  msg = "Model artifact must be attested with cosign before deployment"
}
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you handle key rotation and revocation?
- How would you test end-to-end in CI/CD and cluster?
